short: The input text, instructions, examples, or media provided to a generative model to steer what it produces next.
eli5: The question, request, or starter note you hand to an AI so it knows what job you want done.
example: Asking: 'Summarize this contract in three bullet points for a small-business owner.'

short: Designing clear instructions, roles, constraints, and examples in prompts to get reliable, accurate outputs from language models.
eli5: Learning how to ask crystal-clear questions with helpful context so a bright assistant nails the task on the first try.
example: Specifying output JSON format, edge-case rules, and two worked examples inside a system prompt.

short: Including a handful of input-output examples directly inside the prompt so an LLM infers the pattern without retraining weights.
eli5: Showing someone two completed sample puzzles before handing them a third one to solve.
example: Providing three sample product descriptions and their tone tags before classifying a fourth.

short: Prompting or training a model to break complex problems into intermediate reasoning steps before stating a final answer.
eli5: Showing your scratch-paper math steps out loud instead of blurting out a guess in your head.
example: Solving multi-step word problems or debugging race conditions by tracing variable states line by line.

short: An architecture that retrieves relevant external documents at query time and places them in the prompt before generating an answer.
eli5: Giving the AI an open-book exam where it looks up the exact handbook pages before writing its response.
example: An internal company helpdesk bot citing up-to-date HR policy PDFs instead of guessing from stale memory.

short: A specialized database that stores high-dimensional embeddings and performs fast approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search.
eli5: A smart library that files books by meaning instead of alphabet, instantly handing you the closest topics.
example: Indexing 5 million product manual chunks to retrieve top-5 matches in under 20 milliseconds.

short: Searching a knowledge base using semantic embeddings, keywords, or hybrid scoring to fetch relevant passages for a query.
eli5: Running to the filing cabinet and pulling out only the three folders that actually answer the caller's question.
example: Combining BM25 keyword search with vector cosine similarity to locate exact error codes and guides.

short: Splitting long documents into smaller, overlapping passages so embeddings stay focused and retrieved snippets fit neatly in context.
eli5: Slicing a huge chapter into bite-sized index cards so search finds the exact paragraph instead of the whole book.
example: Splitting Markdown docs by section headings into 400-token chunks with 50-token overlap.

short: A second-stage cross-encoder pass that carefully re-scores top retrieved candidates together with the query for higher precision.
eli5: A quick librarian grabs 20 likely books, then a subject expert skims all 20 and puts the best 3 right on top.
example: Narrowing 50 vector search hits down to the 4 most authoritative passages before LLM generation.

short: An LLM-driven system that plans multi-step goals, invokes external tools, inspects observations, and iterates until a task succeeds.
eli5: Moving from an AI that just answers questions to an assistant that can look things up, run checks, and finish a whole workflow.
example: An engineering agent reading an issue, running unit tests, editing code, and verifying tests pass.

short: Equipping an AI model with external utilities—calculators, web search, databases, or code sandboxes—to overcome static model limits.
eli5: Handing a smart student a calculator and a calendar instead of asking them to multiply huge numbers in their head.
example: Calling a live weather API or SQL database instead of guessing real-time inventory numbers.

short: A structured model capability that outputs typed JSON arguments matching a declared API schema so software can execute actions safely.
eli5: The AI filling out a neat order form with exact fields instead of writing a messy paragraph your code can't parse.
example: Emitting {"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"} to trigger a backend weather lookup function.
